criterion.standard: counts it worthwhile only if the bank actually extends its trust past whoever already has old money behind them
criterion.wasted_life: an account closed on the strength of a family name's absence, not the debt itself
criterion.trusts: a ledger entry - what's actually owed and actually paid, on the page
criterion.distrusts: a family name offered in place of an actual account history

routines.routine_actions: reviews loan applications personally, keeps a running case for every stallholder the bank's standing rules would otherwise turn away
cross-checks the bank's records against the municipal ledgers once a season, on his own initiative

arc.premise: Krastomus is building one real case - around a Dome Market stallholder he's watched work honestly for years, no family name behind them at all - to bring before the bank's senior partners before the season's ledgers close. He means to prove the bank's standing rule against lending past old money wrong, or watch it hold and know exactly what it costs.
